intro: A lighter week of primary-source news. Meta is flipping on an in-app product browsing experience for existing ads by default, Google's Universal Cart brings checkout into AI Mode and Gemini, and Google is steering Demand Gen advertisers toward first-party data. On social, LinkedIn is opening new ways to monetize creator video while Facebook tightens organic link sharing.

stories.summary: Unless an advertiser opts out, tapping a running Facebook or Instagram ad can open an in-app page with product details and suggestions instead of going straight to the landing page. Meta says its own test showed about 3% more conversions, but that figure hasn't been independently verified, and the company had no Help Center article on the change as of mid-October.
stories.takeaway: Decide per client before Oct 28 whether to opt out, especially where landing-page content, tracking or checkout flow matters.
stories.title: Meta will switch on product browsing for existing ads on Oct 28

stories.summary: Shoppers can now save items from AI Mode in Search or the Gemini app into one cross-retailer cart, get price and restock alerts, and check out with Google Pay at participating merchants. It runs on the Universal Commerce Protocol and Google's Shopping Graph, and early retailers include Walmart, Target, Sephora and Nike.
stories.takeaway: Ecommerce clients should check Merchant Center feed quality and ask about Universal Commerce Protocol support, since the cart pulls from Shopping Graph data.
stories.title: Google's Universal Cart starts rolling out in the US

stories.summary: Google is adding a Data Strength Uplift metric that estimates the extra conversions a stronger data setup produced, and is extending Data Manager to Display & Video 360 and Google Analytics. Google credits Tag Gateway setups with a 20%+ conversion uplift, but that comes from its own internal analysis and outside coverage says advertisers can't reproduce it.
stories.takeaway: Use the new metric as a prompt to audit conversion tracking and enhanced conversions, but don't promise clients the 20% number.
stories.title: October Demand Gen Drop puts first-party data front and center

stories.summary: Since Oct 8, Meta no longer accepts ads from ByteDance, or from advertisers whose ads send people to TikTok or other ByteDance apps, in seven markets including the US and Canada. Meta hasn't said whether more countries will follow, and neither company has shared the spend involved. This ran just before the window, but it wasn't covered in last week's issue.
stories.takeaway: Check any Meta ads that link to TikTok profiles, TikTok Shop or TikTok landing pages, since they could be rejected.
stories.title: Meta blocks ads from ByteDance and ads that send people to TikTok

stories.summary: Some Pages and professional accounts now see a prompt capping them at two link posts a month unless they pay for a Meta subscription. Meta frames it as a test of the value of subscriber perks and hasn't published it as a general rule, and reports differ on whether publishers are exempt.
stories.takeaway: Check whether any client Pages are seeing the pop-up, and plan to put links in comments or use paid promotion if organic link posts get capped.
stories.title: Facebook expands its two-link-posts-a-month limit for Pages

stories.summary: LinkedIn is testing pre-roll ads that run on topically relevant creator and publisher videos without a prior partnership, with creators sharing revenue. The update also adds new content insights and in-app one-on-one consultations, though most pieces are invite-only or early testing with no firm dates.
stories.takeaway: Worth asking your LinkedIn rep about the pre-roll test for B2B clients that already invest in thought-leadership video.
stories.title: LinkedIn adds creator monetization, including pre-roll ads on creator video
